body: Round 1 (205fe85c..9a8e2469, five files, .orchestration excluded), Verdict: correct; no P0, P1 or P2. The reviewer checked: path_has_prefix gives the old result for every caller's normalised input and for the root, // and leading-dash edges, with and without strict, and the safe-root guard accepts and refuses exactly as before; python3 -c reads no option after its code, so a path beginning with - cannot inject; normalize_node_path matches Node's path.resolve on 13 cases under bash 3.2 with set -Eeuo pipefail, and update_omp's move-aside, restore and message are unchanged; ensure_crit_cli picks the right artifact for all eight supported uname pairs and skips FreeBSD; all five new tests are red by assertion on 205fe85c and green on 9a8e2469; eight related unit modules are green; the baseline-free lint prints nothing and the seven removed rows are exactly the old lines' hashes; no lint evasion.

Round 1, P3 high: the rows at 950 (update_omp's absolute-or-relative choice) and 211 (is_plugin_data_path's strict check) are behaviour-neutral rewrites; their tests are red at 205fe85c through row 959's HOME fold and the new strict argument, so reverting only those two call sites would keep the tests green. Not changed: no behavioural test can tell a behaviour-neutral rewrite from its original. The guard against such a revert is the lint gate: the rows are gone, so a revert is an unbaselined hit in a changed file, which fails the changed-scope lint and test_lint_comparisons in CI. The report names this beside each row.

Round 1, P3 medium: path_has_prefix now starts one python3 per root and recorded-prefix check, which roughly doubles the guard's process count. Accepted: speed only; the remover already starts python3 for every normalize_* call, so no dependency is new, and a missing python3 makes the guard refuse (fail closed).
Round 1, P3 informational: the absolute-segment check ([ -n "${segment%%/*}" ]) lives inside the normaliser itself; the reviewer judged it acceptable and not lint evasion. No change.
